classification.difficultyReason: Express the square's area algebraically and identify the shaded fraction from its diagonal subdivisions.

content.prompt: Find the area of each shaded region in terms of $a$.

spec.description: Square with bottom and right sides labelled a cm. A diagonal joins bottom-left to top-right. Only the lower-right triangle is shaded. Ordinary source blue strokes become black; meaningful shading uses house light blue.
spec.mathematics: A square of side a cm is divided into two equal-area triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied subdivision and shaded region are visible; no area answer is printed.

answer.worked:
The diagonal divides the square into two equal-area triangles, so the shaded region is half the square.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{square}}&=a\times a\\A_{\text{square}}&=a^2\ \mathrm{cm}^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=\frac{a^2}{2}\ \mathrm{cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Square with top and right sides labelled a cm. Both diagonals meet at the centre. Only the triangle bounded by the top edge and the centre is shaded. Ordinary source blue strokes become black; meaningful shading uses house light blue.
spec.mathematics: The diagonals of a square of side a cm divide it into four equal-area triangles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied subdivisions and shaded region are visible; no area answer is printed.

answer.worked:
The diagonals divide the square into four equal-area triangles, so the shaded region is one quarter of the square.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{square}}&=a\times a\\A_{\text{square}}&=a^2\ \mathrm{cm}^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=\frac{a^2}{4}\ \mathrm{cm}^2\end{align*}$$
